references.text: Joshua is mentioned as Moses' servant, which shows his close relationship with Moses and his role as a leader under Moses' guidance.
Joshua, son of Nun, is identified here, the same person whom Moses commanded to lead the battle against Amalek.
Amalek is mentioned as an enemy Israel fought against, in accordance with the battle described in Exodus 17.
The reminder of what Amalek did to Israel when they came out of Egypt, with a command to blot out the memory of Amalek.
God's staff is mentioned, the same staff Moses held in his hand during the battle against Amalek.
The continuation of the account of the battle against Amalek, where the Lord declares eternal war against Amalek.
The Lord remembers what Amalek did to Israel on the way from Egypt and commands Saul to punish them.
Joshua was from the tribe of Ephraim, and here we see Moses as a shepherd at God's mountain, an image of leadership.
Joshua is mentioned in connection with the rest that was not given, pointing back to his role as leader after Moses.
Both verses illustrate the transition of leadership from Moses to Joshua as a central part of God's story of salvation.
The staff in Moses' hand represents continuous God's power and presence from sign to battle.
Both verses mark steps in Joshua's development as God's chosen leader for Israel.
Parallel between Moses' staff and Joshua's spear as visible signs of God's intervention in conflict.
Shows the transition from Joshua's military mission under Moses to his formal installation as leader.
